item.title: Time to Update Containment Procedures
item.content:encoded:
The current procedures are a bit… outdated.

Item #: SCP-914

Object Class: Safe

Special Containment Procedures: Only personnel who submit a formal request and receive approval from site command may operate 914. SCP-914 is to be kept in research cell 109-B with two guard personnel on duty at all times. Any researchers entering 109-B are to be accompanied by at least one guard for the entirety of testing. A full list of tests to be carried out must be given to all guard personnel on duty; any deviation from this list will result in termination of testing, forcible removal of personnel from 109-B, and formal discipline at site command’s discretion. SCP-914's input and output booths are to be sterilized between tests. Air composition and temperature in research cell 109-B must be monitored at all times during testing. The research cell is to be evacuated and vented if the air becomes uninhabitable or dangerous.

WARNING: At this time, no testing of biological matter is allowed. Refer to document 109-B:117. Applying the “Rough” setting to explosive materials is not advised.

item.title: Re: Relation to 096
item.content:encoded:
Alainpbat, you're effectively (since you seem to have nested the reply incorrectly) replying to a comment that's over five years old.

Furthermore, your suggestion has a couple issues:
1. Dr Dan may be the IRL author, but seeing as we're not a roleplay site, that doesn't make them automatically the person mention in the (in-universe) SCP article.
2. What you mean by "the use of spacial-temporal anomalies to allow coherent events to take place during/before/after" is unclear. Also, how would this improve the article? It seems to be adding unnecessary complicated minutiae details to it.
3. I doubt the Foundation would risk damaging 914, even in the pursuit of terminating 096.
4. There is an assumption being made that 096 could be put into 914 without trouble, and that the result would be worth the effort and eventual trouble.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
By far one of my favorite SCP posts from how intricate the testing is, the callbacks to other SCP's, and the coordination and cooperation between users updating random experiments that yield such a long string of lore to this object. I think this is absolutely deserving to be in the top rated of all time. I also like the constantly unanswered questions, such as exactly how it works, or if it actually has sentience, or how it 'understands' the real implications of the objects.

I'm only curious about more organic tests, despite them being strictly regulated, and where this thing came from. With such a large machine (18 square meters being 4.2 meters each side if it's square, which is over 17 feet is massive). So how did the foundation come to obtain such a mysterious, near-omnipotent machine?

But this is one that has left my mind very expansive. The tie ins to ●●|●●●●●|●●|●, the hilarious realization that the paths are just tracing the SCP logo, the question over how it separates various 1:1 values and why it makes certain things certain times.

I'm so sad how much is redacted or confidential, despite obviously being the intention. I feel like so many questions are unanswered, and it drives me nuts. Truly a good entry though. Knowing how much 914 breaks down objects to rudimentary components in Coarse and Rough settings, I wonder if it'd be a good way to rid ourselves of various Keter-level dangers, like SCP-096. The only failure I believe I remember (because there were a TON of experiments) was when the article on ●●|●●●●●|●●|● was stolen. Everything else was *able* to happen. Also curious what would happen if SCP-988 was somehow able to be put in the input. I'm assuming SCP-988 just wouldn't allow it to happen, but I'm curious.

item.title: Re: Would SCP-914 be able to make things sentient?
item.content:encoded:
To put it another way, yes, there is a chance you could get a sapient robot. This, however, is only one of an infinite number of equally likely outcomes.

That means by simple probability, you are far more likely to get something completely unrelated to what you want the result to be: a decorative robot-themed ash tray, a duplicate of pesterbot, a self-driving moped, a clockwork diorama that enacts the entire plot of Metropolis…

item.title: Re: Would SCP-914 be able to make things sentient?
item.content:encoded:
No.

There's a chance they'd get a sapient robot, and that it's most likely not gonna suit the Foundation's specific needs.

914 is effectively random, and you can barely influence the traits of the outcome, if at all. It's useless to make it mass-produce enhanced objects, since 99% of them aren't gonna be what you want.
